title: Addition
subtitle: in addition, as well as, what's more
summary: Add one point to another in speech and writing using expressions such as in addition, furthermore, as well as, apart from and on top of that.

lesson.heading: Linking two sentences or clauses
lesson.text: These expressions come at the start of the second sentence or clause and simply add another point to the first. **Furthermore** and **moreover** are interchangeable and rather formal; **what's more** is informal (write **what is more** if you want it more formal).

examples.text: For this job you need a degree. **In addition**, you need at least two years' experience.
Smartphones are becoming more sophisticated. **Furthermore**, they are becoming cheaper.
Children should respect their parents. **What's more**, they should respect their teachers.
He's a very good singer. **What is more**, he has a degree in music.

lesson.heading: Adding a point of equal value
lesson.text: **Equally** and **likewise** do not just add a point - they suggest the new point has the same weight as the first. **Equally** is best when you are arguing a case or presenting opinions. **On top of (all) that** is emphatic and mostly used in informal speech.

examples.text: Physical labour can exhaust the body very quickly. **Equally**, excessive study can rapidly reduce mental powers.
My father won't agree. **Likewise**, my mother's sure to find something to object to.
It was raining and getting dark. **On top of all that**, we had very little petrol left in the tank.
To keep fit you need a good diet **plus** regular exercise.
examples.note: plus normally connects noun phrases, but can connect clauses in informal speech

lesson.heading: Expressions at the end of a sentence
lesson.text: Some addition expressions come at the very end. **And so on** is more informal than **etc.**; **and so on and so forth** suggests a long continuation. **Into the bargain** and **to boot** emphasise the combination of items and are both informal.

examples.text: They sell chairs, tables, beds, **and so on**.
It'll go to the committee, then to the board, then to another committee, **and so on and so forth**.
He was a good sportsman and an excellent musician **into the bargain**.
She's a good footballer and a good athlete **to boot**.

lesson.heading: Expressions before a noun or -ing form
lesson.text: These expressions begin or come in the middle of a sentence. They are all followed by a noun, a noun phrase, or a verb plus **-ing** - never by a full clause.

examples.text: **In addition to** winning the gold medal, she also broke the world record.
**As well as** speaking Japanese, she also speaks French.
examples.wrong: As well as she speaks Japanese

examples.text: **Besides** having a salary, he also has a private income.
**Apart from** her many other hobbies, she restores old racing cars.
**Alongside** her full-time job as a dentist, she does voluntary conservation work at weekends.

lesson.heading: Which addition word goes where?
rows: a new sentence or clause of equal value
in addition to, as well as, besides, apart from, alongside
a noun, noun phrase or -ing form

lesson.heading: Adding people and things to a list
lesson.text: **Along with** and **together with** add extra people or things to the ones you have just named. **Further to** is a formal way of opening a letter or an email that follows an earlier one.

examples.text: Jo Evans was there, **along with** a few other people who I didn't know.
My cousin turned up **along with** some schoolmates of his.
**Further to** my telephone call to you yesterday, I am now writing to ...

lesson.text: In a formal letter, vary your addition words - if you have already written *in addition to*, choose *as well as* or *apart from* the next time so you do not repeat yourself.

exercises.prompt: Is each expression informal, or formal / neutral?
Match each addition expression with what it does.

pairs.right: adds a point of the same value

pairs.left: and so on and so forth
pairs.right: suggests a long continuation of a list
opens a formal letter about an earlier one

exercises.prompt: ___ holding a Diploma in Catering, I also have an Advanced Certificate in Hotel Management.
exercises.explanation: These expressions are all followed by a noun, noun phrase or -ing form.

exercises.prompt: The course covered the usual areas: finance, front services, publicity, space allocation, ___.
exercises.explanation: etc. is slightly more formal than and so on, so it suits a job application letter.

exercises.prompt: I have been working in the hotel trade for five years. ___, my experience prior to that was also connected with tourism.
exercises.explanation: Furthermore and moreover add the previous experience on; likewise suggests it is of equal value.

exercises.statement: I work part-time as well as I am a student, so I have a busy life.
exercises.explanation: As well as is followed by an -ing form: I work part-time as well as being a student, so I have a busy life.

exercises.statement: Alongside my many other responsibilities, I now have to be in charge of staff training.
exercises.explanation: Correct - alongside is followed by a noun phrase.

exercises.statement: In addition has a degree, she also has a diploma.
exercises.explanation: In addition to a degree, she also has a diploma. (Or: In addition to having a degree ...)

exercises.statement: Besides to have a good job, my ambition is to meet someone nice to share my life with.
exercises.explanation: Besides having a good job, my ambition is to meet someone nice to share my life with.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct rewrite: 'He owns a big chemical factory and he runs a massive oil business in the USA.' (as well as)
options: He owns a big chemical factory as well as running a massive oil business in the USA.
He owns a big chemical factory as well as he runs a massive oil business in the USA.
He owns a big chemical factory as well as run a massive oil business in the USA.
As well as he owns a big chemical factory, he runs a massive oil business in the USA.
exercises.explanation: As well as takes an -ing form, not a finite clause.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct rewrite: 'I'm their scientific adviser and act as a consultant to the Managing Director.' (addition)
options: In addition to being their scientific adviser, I act as a consultant to the Managing Director.
In addition I am their scientific adviser, I act as a consultant to the Managing Director.
In addition to be their scientific adviser, I act as a consultant to the Managing Director.
In addition of their scientific adviser, I act as a consultant to the Managing Director.
exercises.explanation: In addition to is followed by a noun phrase or an -ing form.

exercises.prompt: He said he'd have to consider the organisation, then the system, then the finance, and so on and so ___.
exercises.explanation: The fixed informal phrase is and so on and so forth.

exercises.answer: My cousin turned up along with some schoolmates of his.
exercises.explanation: Along with adds extra people to the one already mentioned.
